match.reason: The closest bank point covers resources, waste, services and spiritual meaning but never teaches that damage to one function harms the others, which is the central idea of the new point, so it would need a new step rather than a small change.

draft.title: Environmental functions
card: Supply
Environments provide the resources people use, such as water, timber, soil, fish and minerals.
Absorb wastes
Environments take in wastes and break many of them down. Soil, water and air can process some wastes, but only up to a limit.
Support life
Environments keep living things going with clean air, fresh water and a stable climate.
The functions are linked. Damage to one function can harm the others.
draft.remember: Environments supply resources, absorb wastes and support life, and the functions are linked.

a.q: A river gives a town its drinking water and also carries away treated wastewater. Which two environmental functions is the river performing?
opts: Supplying a resource and absorbing wastes
Supplying a resource and supporting a stable climate
Absorbing wastes and supporting a stable climate
Supplying wastes and absorbing resources
a.why: Drinking water is a resource the environment supplies. Carrying away and diluting wastewater is absorbing wastes. The river is not described as affecting climate, so the options that include a stable climate do not fit.
a.clue: One use takes something out. The other puts something in.

b.q: Farmers upstream of a lake in Gippsland clear the land beside it. Soil and fertiliser wash into the lake, and the water becomes unsafe for the town to drink. What does this show?
opts: Damage to one function can harm another function
Lakes cannot absorb any wastes at all
Clearing land harms only the farm's resources
Environmental functions work separately from each other
b.why: The lake took in wastes beyond its limit, and this damaged its ability to supply clean drinking water. So harm to one function harmed another. The card says environments can absorb some wastes, so saying a lake absorbs none is wrong.
b.clue: Look at how the wastes affected the water the town drinks.

a.best: Supplying a resource and absorbing wastes

b.best: Damage to one function can harm another function

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a qualifier ('can') and repeats the card's line word for word. Two distractors use absolutes ('cannot ... at all', 'only'), so a student could pick the answer by test-taking strategy without understanding linked functions.

check.summary: The content is accurate and both answers are clear. In question b, the right option is the only hedged one and copies the card word for word, while two distractors use absolutes, so it can be guessed without knowing the idea.

proposal.title: Environmental functions
card: Supply
Environments provide the resources people use, such as water, timber, soil, fish and minerals.
Absorb wastes
Environments take in wastes and break many of them down. Soil, water and air can process some wastes, but only up to a limit.
Support life
Environments keep living things going with clean air, fresh water and a stable climate.
The functions are linked. Damage to one function can harm the others. For example, smoke from burning rubbish can dirty the air that people and animals breathe.
proposal.remember: Environments supply, absorb and support. Harm one function and the others can suffer.

a.q: A river gives a town its drinking water and also carries away treated wastewater. Which two environmental functions is the river performing?
opts: Supplying a resource and absorbing wastes
Supplying a resource and supporting a stable climate
Absorbing wastes and supporting a stable climate
Supplying wastes and absorbing resources
a.why: Drinking water is a resource the environment supplies. Carrying away and diluting wastewater is absorbing wastes. The river is not described as affecting climate, so the options that include a stable climate do not fit.
a.clue: One use takes something out. The other puts something in.

b.q: Farms upstream of a lake in Gippsland use a lot of fertiliser. Rain washes soil and fertiliser into the lake, and the water becomes unsafe for the town to drink. Which statement best explains this?
opts: Too much waste to absorb harmed its supply of clean water
Too much water supplied harmed its ability to absorb waste
Too much waste to absorb harmed its stable climate
Its waste absorbing and water supply failed independently
b.why: The lake took in more soil and fertiliser than it could absorb, and that waste made its water unsafe, so its supply of clean drinking water was harmed. Saying the two failed independently misses the link: the waste caused the water problem. Nothing in the case is about climate.
b.clue: Ask what made the town's water unsafe.
